title: The Rivergate of the Empty Quarter
premise: Wren Quintana, a storm chaser drowning in debt to the Vane Syndicate, takes a salvage contract to recover a vanished government survey team in the Empty Quarter, a high desert laced with a river that appears on no legal map. Following the river upstream, she discovers the team was murdered to hide an illegal water-diversion scheme run by the Syndicate itself, with her own estranged father's name on the original land grant. Racing the calving glacier that will seal the source canyon for a year, Wren must choose between selling the evidence to erase her debt and giving it to the river towns whose water is being stolen. She floods the diversion works, lets the glacier close the route behind her, and walks out owing nothing but the truth.
about_author: J. M. Pemberton is the pen name of a former hydrological surveyor who spent six seasons mapping ephemeral rivers before turning to fiction. They write from a converted field station, where the tap water is famously undrinkable.

chapters.title: Debt of Clear Skies
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Chasing a supercell in the flats to earn a Syndicate bounty, she calculates that even a perfect season won't cover what she owes. A repo crew waits at her landing strip. Emotional beat: the exhaustion of a life that punishes standing still, and the small pride she takes in reading weather no one else can.

chapters.title: The Contract Nobody Signed
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A fixer named Ovid Hale offers her a salvage job: locate a vanished government survey team, recover their instruments, no questions. The pay clears her debt twice over. She notices the contract lists the survey's last coordinates inside a closed military reserve. Emotional beat: temptation dressed as rescue.

chapters.title: Gear Without Ghosts
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. At the survey's last camp she finds tents pitched, food cached, instruments still logging — and no tracks leaving in any direction, as if the team walked into the river. Emotional beat: the uncanny hush of a place that has decided not to be found.

chapters.title: What the Instruments Recorded
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, intercut with the survey leader's final log entries. The data shows the river's flow dropping impossibly fast upstream, as if something is drinking it. Wren realizes the team wasn't lost; they were getting close to an answer. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Vane Syndicate Sends Regards
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A Syndicate skiff finds her at the camp, and its pilot, Marisol, warns her the salvage contract is a leash, not a lifeline — the Syndicate wants the survey's records destroyed, not recovered. Emotional beat: the sick recognition that she was hired to be the loose end.

chapters.title: Rivergate
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. She reaches a canyon mouth the maps call a dry wash but which runs full and cold — the rivergate, the only passage upstream. Marisol's skiff shadows her. Emotional beat: commitment; she burns her return fuel to keep it from being stolen, choosing forward.

chapters.title: The Town That Isn't on the Ledger
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Upstream she finds Callow's Ferry, an unregistered settlement of surveyors' descendants and water-runners who survive outside every law. Its matriarch, Ida Callow, recognizes the survey team's names. Emotional beat: the warmth of a community that survives by refusing to be counted.

chapters.title: Her Father's Signature
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Ida shows her the original land grant for the diversion scheme — co-signed by Wren's father, the hydrologist who vanished when she was twelve. Emotional beat: grief and fury braided together; the debt she owes is older than money.

chapters.title: Marisol's Bargain
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Ordered to eliminate Wren, Marisol instead reveals the Syndicate has been siphoning the river for a decade, selling water to the very towns it's desiccating, and that the survey team found the proof. Emotional beat: a loyal soldier's conscience cracking under the weight of arithmetic.

chapters.title: The Survey Team's Last Camp
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. High in the gorge she finds the team — or what's left: three graves and a fourth member, Delacroix, half-mad, who survived by hiding and has memorized the evidence because paper can be burned. Emotional beat: the cost of knowing, paid in full.

chapters.title: Calving Season
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The glacier above the source groans; the route through the source canyon opens for roughly nine days before icefall seals it. Ida's runners can move the evidence out, but only if the diversion gates are opened to raise the river for their boats. Emotional beat: the clock made physical — a mountain deciding how long she has.

chapters.title: The Arithmetic of Mercy
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Hale arrives with an offer: her debt erased, her father's name quietly cleared, in exchange for the evidence and Delacroix's silence. Wren almost takes it. Emotional beat: the seductive logic of a clean transaction over a dirty justice.

chapters.title: What Water Owes
chapters.summary: Ida's POV. Ida refuses to let Callow's Ferry become complicit in a trade — the town has survived by taking in strays, not selling them. She puts the town's boats at Wren's disposal. Emotional beat: inheritance redefined as obligation to the living, not the dead.

chapters.title: The Ascent of the Source Canyon
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren, Marisol, and Delacroix climb toward the diversion works as the glacier begins shedding ice into the gorge behind them. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into rhythm — each step timed to the mountain's breathing.

chapters.title: The Machinery of Thirst
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. At the source they find the diversion headworks: a hidden dam and pumping station, staffed and armed, siphoning the river into Syndicate canals. Wren's father's engineering drawings hang in the control room like scripture. Emotional beat: horror at how neatly theft can be dressed as infrastructure.

chapters.title: Hale's Last Optimism
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. Hale, cornered, confesses the Syndicate's founders were idealists who believed controlling water meant saving everyone — and that Wren's father tried to blow the whistle and was erased for it. Emotional beat: the tragedy of power corrupting its own believers.

chapters.title: Opening the Gates
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The climax: under icefall fire, Wren and Marisol sabotage the pumps and blow the diversion gates, sending the stolen river back down the gorge to lift Ida's boats. Hale drowns trying to save the ledgers. Emotional beat: fury released as an act of restoration, not revenge.

chapters.title: The Mountain Closes the Door
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The calving seals the source canyon behind them, burying the evidence's original site and any chance of a clean legal case — only testimony remains. Emotional beat: the strange peace of a door closing on the past.

chapters.title: Delacroix Testifies
chapters.summary: Delacroix's POV. In Callow's Ferry, Delacroix recounts everything to an assembled crowd of river towns, and Ida's runners carry copies of the recovered logs downstream ahead of the Syndicate's lawyers. Emotional beat: fragile hope — truth moving faster than money for once.

chapters.title: The Reckoning at Vane
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol delivers the evidence to a federal water tribunal, trading her own immunity for the names of every Syndicate principal. Emotional beat: a soldier choosing the harder sentence — accountability over absolution.

chapters.title: What Wren Owes Now
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The tribunal voids her debt as proceeds of an illegal enterprise; her father's name is posthumously cleared. Ida offers her a place in Callow's Ferry, and Wren, for the first time, considers stopping. Emotional beat: learning that a debt paid is also a door opened.

chapters.title: The River, Unmapped
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, epilogue. A year later, Wren runs a storm-chasing and river-guide outfit out of Callow's Ferry, teaching the next generation to read both weather and water. The river runs free to the towns. Emotional beat: quiet resolution — she has inherited not a fortune but a current, and she keeps it moving.
